title: MegaMmap: Blurring the Boundary Between Memory and Storage for Data-Intensive Workloads
problem: Data-intensive HPC workloads exceeding main memory capacity suffer from severe data movement penalties, programming complexity, and limited code reuse in out-of-core algorithms.
motivation: Cost-effective and sustainable memory expansion through intelligent storage management is needed as continuously increasing DRAM capacity is financially and environmentally unsustainable.
method: MegaMmap creates a single unified memory view across your computer's fast RAM and slower storage (like SSDs), letting you write programs as if all your data fits in RAM even when it doesn't. It watches how your program uses data and automatically moves frequently-accessed information into fast RAM while pushing rarely-used data to storage. To avoid slowdowns, it predicts which data you'll need next and brings it into fast memory ahead of time, using hints about critical data to keep the fast and slow memory layers in sync.
key_novelty: The core innovation is software that automatically moves data between fast RAM and slow storage based on actual program usage, making them work as a single unified memory system.
contributions: Software distributed shared memory for multi-tiered DRAM and storage management
Workload-aware data organization and eviction policies reducing DRAM consumption
Memory coherence optimization through intuitive hinting system
Demonstration of competitive performance with significantly reduced DRAM requirements
limitations: Specific performance baselines, scalability limits, and trade-offs not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Distributed shared memory with intelligent tiering
